clue.text: Can wobble through missing handlebar on your bike?

indicators.note: through says the shaken letters run through the middle of the other piece

parts.note: missing something means having no such thing, so no
a handlebar is a style of moustache, a tache in British slang

indicators.note: to wobble is to be unsteady, so the letters of the word can are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A cyclist asks whether a tin can roll through a gap left by a lost handlebar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobble' turns CAN into ANC, which goes 'through' NOTACHE. 'Handlebar' looks like part of a bicycle, but it is a moustache; TACHE is British slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: 'On your bike!' is British slang telling someone to go away, a blunt refusal, like the phrase meaning 'no way'.

clue.text: Nut-burying type heading off army — that's ironic

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
'that's rich' is said of a remark one finds ironic

explanation.surface: A squirrel-like creature evading soldiers, with a wry aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is slang for head; this bird is said to bury its head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famed, wrongly, for hiding its head in sand when in danger, and nut is slang for head.

clue.text: Jittery 28 secures English Test Series

indicators.note: secures says the jumbled letters hold another piece inside
jittery means shaky, so the letters of the other answer are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 28 Across is a band of cloth

explanation.surface: A nervous player gripping the trophy in an England cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jittery' turns SASH into ASHS, which 'secures' E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the cricket Test series played between England and Australia.

clue.text: Outcome in woman's cooking for friend of Bigfoot

indicators.note: in says the outcome goes inside the woman's word

parts.note: a woman's belongings are hers
an outcome is an end
food that is cooking is on

explanation.surface: The result of a woman's recipe is meant for Bigfoot's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film Harry and the Hendersons, a family befriend a Bigfoot creature.

clue.text: Half of student jazz singer's story, short one

indicators.note: half of says take the first three of six letters from the word for a learner

parts.note: a novice is a learner or beginner
Ella Fitzgerald was a great jazz singer

explanation.surface: Half a student's tale about a jazz singer, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: Newspaper about to carry letter on 20's creator

indicators.note: on in a down clue says this piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: el is the name of the letter L

indicators.note: about says the word is turned round

parts.note: a rag is a disreputable newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper is about to print a letter on a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAG into GAR. 20 Across, NIMROD, is the best-known of the Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote the Enigma Variations, whose ninth movement is the famous Nimrod.

clue.text: One's first label: Killer

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word One

parts.note: RCA is a well-known record label

explanation.surface: Reads like a note on a record sleeve or a band's debut release called Killer.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is the common name for this black-and-white marine predator.

clue.text: Sitcoms broadcast about artist's isolation

indicators.note: about says the scattered letters go round the other piece
broadcast also means scattered, so the letters of sitcoms are spread anew

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: TV comedies aired about a painter leave them cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns SITCOMS into OSTCISM, set 'about' RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from a group or society, leaving someone shunned and alone.

clue.text: Film about king, one with a country

indicators.note: about says the layer goes round the king

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, a coat
R stands for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A movie about a monarch and a companion visiting a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in south-eastern Europe on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Nameless thing given award to burn

parts.note: a thing left unnamed is simply 'it'
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: Something anonymous is honoured with a prize and then set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn to do something is to long for it eagerly, a sense of strong desire shared by both words.

clue.text: Gutted about piercing Giovanni? Nasty cut

indicators.note: piercing says those two letters stab into the middle of the other piece
nasty signals that the letters of the name Giovanni are messed up and rearranged
gutted means the insides are removed, so only the outside letters of the word about are kept

explanation.surface: Don Giovanni, devastated, is wounded by a vicious knife cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' keeps only the outer letters, and 'piercing' pushes them into NAVIGION, the 'Nasty' rearrangement. 'Cut' is not a wound: it is an old word for a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a cut is a man-made canal, and canals were once called navigations, being waterways dug for barges.

clue.text: Right wrong?

parts.note: 'right' sounds like 'write', so writing something wrong means getting its letters wrong

explanation.surface: A two-word moral puzzle: can something right also be wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is read as the verb 'write', said the same way; to write wrongly is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a word incorrectly is exactly the error of bad spelling, which the question cryptically describes.

clue.text: A foreign currency for exchange

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and Oman
for in the sense 'for the purpose of' can be swapped for to

explanation.surface: Someone at a bureau de change offering foreign money to swap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto in Venice was the city's merchants' exchange, and the name has come to mean any market.

clue.text: Transport needs to be announced for island

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so we want a word that is said the same way

parts.note: road transport needs highways to run on, so roads

explanation.surface: A notice that a ferry or bus for an island will be announced soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, the largest of the Dodecanese group.

clue.text: It's run on gas, this Devon town

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
gas is chatter, and mouth is idle talk

explanation.surface: A boast that a seaside town's buses run on gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth is a harbour town in Devon, home of the Royal Navy's officer college.

clue.text: Ultimate competitor's run out of records?

parts.note: arch means chief or ultimate, as in arch-enemy

indicators.note: out says the letter for run is dropped from the longer phrase

parts.note: a competitor is a rival
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Sports commentary: has the greatest opponent finally been run out, ending the record books?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like cricket, but 'out' simply removes R from RIVAL, leaving IVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archival belongs to or is kept in archives, the stored documents of an institution.

clue.text: Fish circles type of buoy — unusual problem

indicators.note: circles says the fish surrounds the buoy

parts.note: cod is a common fish
a nun buoy is a conical marker buoy
rum means odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A fish swimming round a buoy is a strange problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling problem or riddle that is hard to resolve.

clue.text: Logical expressions also found in 'illogical' prose

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other
illogical says the letters of prose are put in a senseless new order

parts.note: also and and both add one thing to another

explanation.surface: A comment that logical statements turn up even in irrational writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illogical' shuffles the prose into OPERS, which then holds the conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and maths, operands are the quantities or terms an operator acts upon in an expression.

clue.text: This predator is old man around country hotel

indicators.note: around says the father goes round the other pieces

parts.note: pa is father, one's old man
Iran is a country
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grandfather predator lurking about a country hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a sharp-toothed carnivorous South American freshwater fish.

clue.text: Ineptly tries to cross dry passages

indicators.note: to cross here means to span, putting the jumbled letters around the other piece
ineptly says the letters of tries are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily attempts to cross arid stretches of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ineptly' gives STREI, which goes across the abbreviation for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti are the overlapping fugue entries of a musical theme, so musical passages.

clue.text: Angler chasing game, a hunter

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matches or counters from piles
an angler is a rod, from rod and line

explanation.surface: A fisherman pursuing wild animals turns out to be a mighty huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the biblical 'mighty hunter before the Lord', and his name is used for any keen hunter.

clue.text: Extended programme: Wrestling rings throw out retired?

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the whole thing is turned round
rings says the wrestling word surrounds the other

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
to bin something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: Wrestlers in the ring ejecting a retired fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' gives SUBINMO, and 'retired' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers a week's episodes into one long broadcast.

clue.text: To attract doctor, official carries uniform

indicators.note: carries says the official holds the other letter inside

parts.note: an ump, short for umpire, is a sports official
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A medic and an umpire in uniform trying to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum up custom or support is to attract it by persistent effort.

clue.text: Track down detective, one out of position

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: out of says the numeral is removed

parts.note: a site is a position
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Hunting down a detective who has been moved from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track down' looks like a verb meaning find; it is a ski track that runs downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared ski run, a track you go down on skis.

clue.text: Imperative for leaving top taken from shop in bar?

indicators.note: in says the shortened shop sits inside the bar

parts.note: a rung is a bar of a ladder

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: a salon is a shop, such as a hairdresser's

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what a barman says when someone leaves a shop inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top taken from' turns SALON into ALON, which goes 'in' RUNG. 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a ladder step.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a command telling someone, often a child, to go away or leave now.

clue.text: Honest soldier kept in check

indicators.note: kept in says the soldier is held inside

parts.note: a let is a hindrance or check, as in 'without let or hindrance'
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A truthful soldier held in restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, meaning lawful and above-board.

clue.text: One prize crossword selected is tackled by desert troops

parts.note: someone selected for a team is in

indicators.note: tackled by says the word is is held inside the other

parts.note: to desert is to quit
taken as written
OR, other ranks, are ordinary troops in the British army

explanation.surface: A soldiers' raid on a chosen prize puzzle in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert troops' reads as one army unit, but desert is a verb here and troops are other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inquisitor is the Independent's weekly prize puzzle, a thematic barred crossword.

clue.text: Nearly pass one in the desert

indicators.note: nearly says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to go by is to pass
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Almost walking past a lone figure in a wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Somewhat serious as hip-hop band

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describes a music group whose sound is rather earnest, in the style of rap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: One setting puzzle — I am setting cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure, so the letters of these words are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A setter introduces themselves while composing a cryptic crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter of puzzles, especially cryptic crosswords, is a maker of riddles or enigmas.
